literal: Than sleeping on the soft shoulders of one's beloved, is it sweeter, the world of the lotus-eyed one?
translation: Is the world of the lotus-eyed deity any sweeter than slumbering on the soft shoulders of one's beloved?
modern: தாம் விரும்பும் காதலியின் மென்மையான தோள்களில் துயில்வதை விட, தாமரை போன்ற கண்களை உடைய இறைவனின் உலகம் இனிமையானதோ?
explanation: In this couplet, the speaker compares the ultimate spiritual or celestial bliss with the intimate joy of love. The phrase 'tām vīḻvār' refers to the beloved whom one desires, and 'meṉṟōḷ' describes her soft shoulders. By questioning whether the realm of the lotus-eyed deity is sweeter than sleeping in the embrace of the beloved, the poem exalts earthly love as a supreme experience that rivals or even surpasses divine realms.
